title: Disinfection Practices

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

summary: Applying an appropriate chemical or physical agent to reduce pathogenic microorganisms on surfaces or equipment to a safer level.
explanation: Effective disinfection depends on selecting an agent appropriate to the likely contaminating organisms, using it at the concentration and for the contact time specified by the product/method (both of which vary by product and are not universal), and ensuring the surface is compatible with the agent. Not every disinfectant is sporicidal at routinely used concentrations — see the Sterilization vs. Disinfection concept entry.
keyPractices: Choose a disinfectant appropriate to the likely organisms and surface material.
Follow the specific product's stated concentration and contact time — do not assume a universal number applies across products.
Allow the full contact time before wiping/rinsing.
Ventilate appropriately when using volatile disinfectants.
commonMistakes: Wiping a surface immediately after applying disinfectant, without allowing the full contact time to elapse.
